hot.pointer_line: On now: the last humpbacks and the first possible whale sharks, a windless gap before the kaskazi, short rains forecast above average from mid-October, full moons on 26 October and 24 November, Mashujaa Day on 20 October, and a dance festival at Safari Beach on 11-18 November.

items.name: The humpbacks are leaving
items.teaser: The humpback window is closing: the operators' dedicated whale trips ended with September
items.story: Humpbacks swim up from the Southern Ocean to breed and calve in East African water, then turn south with their calves. The IWC's whale-watching handbook puts them on the Kenya coast between August and October, and a Watamu operator describes the return south with calves around October. Diani's own whale expeditions ran 15 August to 30 September this year. In mid-October a whale is still possible on any boat that goes outside the reef. By November it would be luck. Book a reef or dolphin trip that might meet one; nobody should be selling you a whale trip now.
items.why: A mid-October boat outside the reef can still meet a mother and calf heading south, but treat it as a bonus.
facts: Coast season about Aug-Oct; dedicated Diani whale trips ran 15 Aug-30 Sep 2026; occasional into Nov at best
Outside the reef off Diani and Galu
Ask whether the boat carries a hydrophone: Whale Shark Adventures has used one to play the song aboard

items.name: Whale sharks: early, not peak
items.teaser: The first whale sharks can turn up from October, but the reliable months are January to March
items.story: This coast's whale-shark season is usually given as October to March, and the sources lean late: the research expeditions of the East African Whale Shark Trust traditionally ran from February to mid-March, and Diani operators name February and March as the best months. Early arrivals do happen; one season opened in October. So in October and November a sighting is possible, not likely. Ocean Tribe said on its own page that it was not running whale-shark trips for 2025/26; Whale Shark Adventures uses a spotter plane in its stated windows. If whale sharks are the reason, come in the new year.
items.why: Book a reef day that might meet one now; save the dedicated spotter-plane trip for the new year.
facts: Possible from Oct; best Jan-Mar (sources differ on the peak)
Diani to Kisite, outside the reef
Ask the operator for this season's actual sightings before paying, not last year's photos

items.name: No kite wind until mid-December
items.teaser: October and November are the gap between the two monsoons: the kite schools have nothing to teach
items.story: The southerly kusi, which blew from June, has faded. The northeasterly kaskazi is not due until about mid-December. H2O Extreme's own wind page says plainly that outside the two windows, roughly April-May and October-November, there is no lesson to give. The gap has its uses. With the kusi gone the sea goes slack and clear: Ocean Tribe gives October to March as its diving months. The flat lagoon is better for paddleboards and snorkelling than for kites. The first steady kaskazi days, usually from the second half of December, reopen the schools at Galu.
items.why: Come in October or November to dive and paddle; come after mid-December to kite.
facts: Kaskazi about mid-Dec to mid-Mar (15-20 knots, filling in around 10:30); kusi Jun to mid-Sep
Galu, the south end of the strip, where both kite schools sit
If a gusty day turns up in November, ask the school before assuming it is on

items.name: Full moons on 26 October and 24 November
items.teaser: Full moon Mon 26 Oct at 07:12 and Tue 24 Nov at 17:53 East Africa Time: the lowest lows of each month
items.story: The full moon falls at 04:12 UTC on 26 October, which is 07:12 in Diani, and at 14:53 UTC on 24 November, 17:53 local time. November's is a supermoon. The spring tides on the days either side give the widest low water of the month, and the lagoon inside the reef drains far enough to walk the flats; the new moons of 10 October and 9 November do the same. These are the bamvua mornings of the fishers' calendar, told in the sea section. Read a tide table for the exact low before you set out: the hour shifts by about 50 minutes a day.
items.why: The reef walk and the dawn landing are both worth planning around these dates.
facts: Full moon Mon 26 Oct, 07:12 EAT; Tue 24 Nov, 17:53 EAT (supermoon). New moon 9 Nov
The whole lagoon, Tiwi to Chale
Walk the flats on the falling tide and turn back before the flood; wear reef shoes

items.name: Orionids and Leonids
items.teaser: Orionids peak the night of 21-22 Oct, Leonids 17-18 Nov; both are best in the hours before dawn
items.story: The Orionids, dust from Halley's Comet, peak on the night of 21-22 October. A waxing gibbous moon, about 80 per cent lit, washes out the evening, so wait until it sets after midnight; the hours before dawn are the dark ones. Expect up to about 20 meteors an hour in ideal sky, fewer here. The Leonids peak on the night of 17-18 November (one calendar says 16-17), at about 10 an hour, with the moon setting before the best hours. The short rains may cloud either night. There is no eclipse in October or November 2026.
items.why: You need nothing but a dark stretch of sand away from the hotel lights and 20 minutes without a phone screen.
facts: Orionids night of 21-22 Oct; Leonids night of 17-18 Nov; both best pre-dawn
Any dark stretch of beach; the sea horizon is east

items.name: The short rains, forecast above average
items.teaser: Kenya Met puts Kwale in the above-average rain group, with onset in the second to third week of October
items.story: The Kenya Meteorological Department issued its October-December outlook at the end of August 2026. It lists Kwale and Mombasa among the counties expected to get above-average rainfall, and it forecast onset on the coast in the second to third weeks of October, with prolonged wet spells and occasional isolated storms. The forecasters tied the season to El Nino and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole, and used 2015 as an analogue year. Their own director cautioned that El Nino does not mean heavy rain everywhere. On this coast the short rains usually arrive as heavy afternoon or night showers rather than days of grey.
items.why: Keep an indoor fallback for the afternoons and allow extra time on the Likoni road.
facts: Onset forecast mid to late Oct; season Oct-Dec 2026

items.name: The first mangoes
items.teaser: Coast mangoes start in November; the big harvest is December to March
items.story: Coast Province is Kenya's main mango region, and the season that matters here starts as the short rains begin. A Malindi guide gives the coast's own Ngowe variety a November-to-March harvest, with Apple mangoes from December; the older notes in this guide put Ngowe at its best in December and January. Kenyan sources describe the high season as October to March overall, and most of the picking happens from December. So in November the first fruit is real but thin on the stalls. Ask the trader what came in this week and where it was grown.
items.why: The first local fruit of November tastes different from the imported mango that fills the gap months.
facts: First fruit Nov; main harvest Dec-Mar; Ngowe best Dec-Jan

items.name: Pweza at the bamvua landings
items.teaser: Octopus comes in on the spring-tide mornings around 26 Oct and 24 Nov, and the new moon of 9 Nov
items.story: Most of the octopus on this coast is gathered on foot on the low-tide reef flats, and the gleaners work the spring tides. That makes landings heaviest in the days around full and new moon: in this window, 26 October, 9 November and 24 November. Buy at Mwaepe on the morning tide, judge by eye, pay cash, and cook it the coast's way in coconut.
items.why: Supply follows the moon, not a season: time the fish run to the spring tides.
facts: Pweza and whole reef fish off the boats
06:00-09:00 on the incoming tide, around 26 Oct, 9 Nov and 24 Nov

items.name: Mashujaa Day, Tuesday 20 October
items.teaser: Heroes' Day is a national holiday; the main parade is in Eldoret, and the beach strip carries on
items.story: Mashujaa Day honours the Kenyans who fought for independence and since. It is a public holiday on 20 October, a Tuesday this year. The national celebrations in 2026 are co-hosted for the first time by three Rift Valley counties, with the main event at Kipchoge Keino Stadium in Eldoret, far from the coast. In Diani, hotels, bars and boats run as normal. Banks, county offices and anything needing a government stamp close. The previous public holiday, Mazingira Day, fell on Saturday 10 October.
items.why: Do bank, KWS or county errands on the Monday.
facts: Withdraw cash or top up M-Pesa the day before

items.name: DanSafari dance week at Safari Beach
items.teaser: Listings put an African social-dance festival at Safari Beach Hotel from Wed 11 to Wed 18 Nov
items.story: Two ticketing listings put the DanSafari festival at Safari Beach Hotel in Diani from 11 to 18 November 2026: workshops by day, social dancing and parties at night, and an African social-dance championship. One listing gives prices from KES 2,000 for a single competition division to KES 6,000 for an early-bird festival pass, with travel packages sold separately. We found no official festival website, so treat the details as provisional and confirm with the organiser before you plan around it.
items.why: The one dated event on the south coast in this window.
facts: KES 2,000 single division to KES 6,000 early-bird pass (listing, seen Oct 2026; unconfirmed)

items.name: Otherwise, nothing scheduled
items.teaser: Apart from the dance week, we found no festival or regatta on this coast in October or November 2026
items.story: We looked. The film festival ran in July and August, the Colobus golf day in September, and the skydiving boogie flew in March. No Diani fishing tournament or regatta survived checking, and the December beach festival has no recent dated edition. No skydiving boogie is announced for the rest of 2026. The next public holiday after Mashujaa Day is Jamhuri Day, Saturday 12 December. This is the quiet stretch between the kusi and the December crowd: empty sand, lower room prices, calm water.
items.why: Come for the sea and the prices, not for an event.
facts: 11 Oct-30 Nov 2026: nothing else confirmed (checked Oct 2026)

items.name: Diani Film Festival
items.teaser: Started to answer Diani's lack of cinemas; the 2026 edition ran late July into August
items.story: The festival was founded to address the shortage of cinemas in Kenya and in Diani in particular. Its second edition ran 24-27 July 2026 at Safari Beach Resort in Diani, with an opening screening at Ukunda Showground on 23 July, then moved to Cinemax in Nyali for 31 July and 1 August. Admission was listed as free. The Kenya Film Commission reported the winners: Jua Kali by Joash Omondi took Best African Short Film, and each winner received KES 100,000. Dates for 2027 have not been announced.
items.why: If you are here in late July, it is the one place on the coast to see new African short film.
facts: Safari Beach Resort, Diani; Ukunda Showground; Cinemax, Nyali

items.name: Golf on the Beach for the colobus
items.teaser: Colobus Conservation's beach golf day, every September, pays for the rope bridges over the road
items.story: Colobus Conservation runs a golf day on the sand each September as its main public fundraiser, part of its annual Colobus Awareness Day. The 2025 edition was on 7 September at Nomad Beach Bar on Diani Beach Road. The 12th, by the charity's announcement seen in August, was set for 20 September 2026 at Nomad, adults KES 1,000. Earlier editions paid for the vet clinic and for maintaining the colobridges, the rope crossings over the beach road. Nobody needs to play well. The 2027 date is not yet published.
items.why: A cheap, sociable September Sunday that funds something you can see from the road.
facts: September; 2026 edition 20 Sep (seen Aug 2026); 2027 not yet dated
Nomad Beach Bar & Restaurant, Diani Beach Road

items.name: Skydiving boogies
items.teaser: Diani hosts skydiving boogies, but they are announced late; the last one flew in March 2026
items.story: Diani's beach has drawn skydivers since the December beach festivals of the late 2010s. The Kenya Boogie 2026 flew in March from a Cessna Caravan at 12,000 feet, landing on the sand in front of Diamonds Leisure, and was the first organised HALO jumping in the country. A 2020 boogie had about 60 jumpers. None is announced for the rest of 2026. Watch the skydiving press and Skydive Swahili, which flies tandems at Blue Marlin from Thursday to Monday the rest of the year.
items.why: Watching a boogie from the beach is free and good to see; a tandem is bookable any week.
facts: No fixed month; last: March 2026; next: not announced (checked Oct 2026)

items.name: The Diani Beach Festival
items.teaser: A December beach festival ran in the late 2010s; we found no dated edition since
items.story: From 2017 to 2019 the Diani Beach Festival filled December: a month of skydiving and sport from about 9 December and a three-day beach party at the end of the month, with organisers promising more than 15,000 visitors. We could not find a dated edition for 2025 or 2026, and some December listings mention it with no year. Assume the beach is busy from mid-December through New Year whether or not a festival is billed, and book rooms early for that fortnight.
items.why: December is high season either way; do not plan a trip around this festival unless a date is published.
facts: December in 2017-2019; no edition dated since (checked Oct 2026)

items.name: Kenya's national days
items.teaser: Madaraka 1 June, Mazingira 10 Oct, Mashujaa 20 Oct, Jamhuri 12 Dec: banks close, the beach does not
items.story: Kenya's fixed civic holidays are Madaraka Day on 1 June, for self-rule in 1963; Mazingira Day on 10 October; Mashujaa (Heroes') Day on 20 October; and Jamhuri Day on 12 December, for independence and the republic. When one falls on a Sunday, the Monday after is a day off. In 2027 Madaraka is a Tuesday, Mashujaa a Wednesday, and Jamhuri a Sunday with Monday 13 December off. Sources disagree on whether 26 December is now Utamaduni Day. On every one of these, hotels and boats work and offices shut.
items.why: Check the list before any trip that needs a bank, KWS office or county permit.
facts: 1 Jun, 10 Oct, 20 Oct, 12 Dec; Sunday holidays move to Monday
Do paperwork the day before; ATMs at Ukunda can run dry on long weekends

items.name: Ramadan and Idd, 2027
items.teaser: Ramadan is expected to start around 8 February 2027, Idd ul-Fitr around 9-10 March: approximate, by the moon
items.story: Most of Diani's Digo and Swahili neighbours are Muslim, and Ramadan reshapes the coast's day. It is expected to begin around Monday 8 February 2027 and to last 29 or 30 days, so Idd ul-Fitr, a Kenyan public holiday, is projected for about 9-10 March. Both depend on sighting the new moon and are confirmed only the evening before. During the month, local kitchens close by day and the towns eat at dusk; plan around iftar. Eid al-Adha is projected for about 16-17 May 2027; we could not confirm it is a public holiday that year.
items.why: Ukunda's evening food comes alive after sunset during Ramadan.
facts: Ramadan about 8 Feb-9 Mar 2027; Idd ul-Fitr about 9-10 Mar; Eid al-Adha about 16-17 May (all approximate)

items.name: Sea Turtle Festival
items.teaser: A free community festival on or near World Sea Turtle Day, 16 June, now in its seventh year
items.story: Diani's Sea Turtle Festival is held each June on or close to World Sea Turtle Day, 16 June, and is free. The second edition was at Safari Beach on 13 June 2021, the fifth in 2024, and the sixth was set for 16 June. Our August 2026 check found the seventh edition held at Diamonds Leisure in June 2026. Organisers open applications for art entries ahead of it. Diani Turtle Watch, which patrols the beach each morning and moves at-risk nests, is the programme to support the rest of the year.
items.why: The one day the turtle programme is a party rather than a dawn patrol.
facts: Mid-June, near 16 Jun; 2027 date not yet published
Diani; recent venues Safari Beach and Diamonds Leisure

items.name: The two monsoons
items.teaser: The northeasterly kaskazi blows mid-Dec to mid-Mar; the southerly kusi June to mid-Sep; the gaps are calm
items.story: The coast's year is set by two trade winds. The kaskazi blows from the north and northeast from about mid-December to mid-March at 15-20 knots: hot, steady, dry, with clear water and the best kiting for beginners. The kusi blows from the south and southeast from about June to mid-September at 18-22 knots: cooler, gustier, wetter crossings, and the season for tuna and trevally. Between them, in April-May and October-November, the wind drops and the long and short rains fall. For centuries the same winds timed the dhow trade: down from Arabia on the kaskazi, home on the kusi.
items.why: Pick your month by what you want the sea to do.
facts: Kaskazi mid-Dec-mid-Mar; kusi Jun-mid-Sep; calm gaps Apr-May and Oct-Nov
Kisite visibility is best Oct-Mar; the kusi chop cuts it Jun-Aug

items.name: Whales and whale sharks by month
items.teaser: Humpbacks August to October; whale sharks possible from October, best January to March
items.story: Humpbacks pass the Kenya coast on their breeding migration from about July or August to October, peaking in August and September; the Diani operators' dedicated whale trips ran 15 August to 30 September in 2026. Whale sharks follow from about October, with most sources putting the best months in January to March and research expeditions traditionally in February to mid-March. The two seasons overlap briefly in October, and boats have seen both on the same day. Neither is guaranteed. Pay for a search, not a sighting.
items.why: Humpbacks for an August trip, whale sharks for February: do not book either out of season.
facts: Humpbacks about Aug-Oct; whale sharks Oct-Mar, best Jan-Mar
Outside the reef, Diani to Kisite

listening.name: No listening bar: go for the live nights
listening.teaser: No vinyl or hi-fi listening bar in Diani or Ukunda as of October 2026; the strip does live nights instead
listening.story: We searched for a listening bar, record bar or hi-fi room in Diani and Ukunda and found none as of October 2026. What the strip has is live nights on a weekly rhythm, all from venues in this guide and last checked in August 2026. Funky Monkey's Wednesday is Hot Salsa night with DJs. Skippers Coliving has live music on Thursdays, but it is a residents' base, and outsiders should ask first. Asha's Friday all-you-can-eat barbecue comes with live guitar. The 41 Beach Club lists live jazz, and Pallet Cafe at Galu has music on Sundays.
listening.why: Use the week: salsa Wednesday, live music Thursday, guitar Friday, jazz at the weekend.
facts: Funky Monkey (Wed); Skippers Coliving (Thu, ask first); Asha Bistro (Fri); The 41 Beach Club; Pallet Cafe, Galu (Sun)
Funky Monkey runs to midnight Wed-Sat; other times unpublished

notes: WebFetch blocked; every new fact comes from WebSearch result extracts of the cited pages, not first-hand page reads. Kenya Met OND 2026: Kwale/Mombasa above-average and coastal onset in weeks 2-3 of October come from the KMD PDFs as summarised in search and Capital FM; the county onset table itself was not read. Whale sharks: no 2026 sighting report found; season framing is Oct-Mar with the peak given variously as Jan-Feb (old guide) or Feb-Mar (Coral Spirit, EAWST expedition window). Ocean Tribe's 'not running 2025/26' line is from the August venue record. Humpbacks: the 15 Aug-30 Sep operator window is from the August board; IWC gives Aug-Oct. DanSafari 11-18 Nov 2026 at Safari Beach Hotel rests on two third-party listings (Ticket Fairy, AllEvents); no official site; prices unconfirmed. Sea Turtle Festival: 7th edition at Diamonds Leisure June 2026 comes from the old August-verified card; search found only the 2nd (2021, Safari Beach), 5th (2024) and an undated 6th (16 June). Colobus Golf on the Beach 2026 (12th, 20 Sep, Nomad, KES 1,000) comes from the old card; search only confirmed the 2025 edition (7 Sep, Nomad). Whether the 2026 one went ahead is unverified. Diani Beach Festival: no edition dated after 2019 found. No December 2026 skydiving boogie found. Mango timing conflicts slightly: Ngowe Nov-Mar (Malindi guide) vs Dec-Jan peak (old guide); both are given. Leonid peak night: most sources 17-18 Nov, one AMS line 16-17 Nov. Leonid moon described only as setting before the best hours. 'No eclipse in Oct-Nov 2026' rests on the 2026 eclipse list (Feb, Mar, Aug); EclipseWise cited but not re-read. Eid al-Adha 2027 public-holiday status in Kenya unconfirmed; Utamaduni Day (26 Dec) is listed by one source only and is flagged as disputed. Mazingira Day naming for 10 Oct varies by source. Listening bar: none found; the live nights (Funky Monkey Wed salsa, Skippers Thu, Asha Fri guitar, 41 Beach Club jazz, Pallet Cafe Sun) are from the August 2026 venue records, not rechecked now. No current octopus reef closure on the Diani-Chale reef was searched for; the pweza card makes no closure claim.
